section.t: B"S.
20 Menachem-Av 5737*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you but to fear..." and the Gemara's interpretation of "mah" as "me'ah" (one hundred).
section.t: "And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you but to fear [Him]..."
And it is brought in the Gemara:
It was taught: Rabbi Meir would say, "A person is obligated to recite one hundred blessings every day, as it is said, 'And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you.'"
Do not read "mah" (what) but rather "me'ah" (one hundred).
And it may be said
that the reason for this, that they expounded "do not read 'mah' etc.," is
because according to the simple interpretation, an explanation is needed:
Why does the verse state this matter
(that Hashem your G-d asks of you only to fear, etc.)
in the style of a question and answer,
for ostensibly it should have said, "Hashem your G-d does not ask of you anything but to fear, etc."
Therefore they expounded: Do not read "mah" but rather "me'ah."
And it is known
in the general principles of the study of "do not read,"
that it does not negate the plain meaning of the matter as it is read, but rather adds another interpretation,
and the two interpretations are connected to each other.
And one must understand the connection and relationship between "mah" and "me'ah."
And particularly since the difference between the two interpretations is
(not only in this word itself,
but)
also in the entirety of the verse.
For according to its simple meaning, it is that He asks for nothing but fear,
but according to the Gemara's interpretation,
"mah"
(one hundred blessings)
is the thing that Hashem your G-d asks of you.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the simple meaning is achieved through the content of the Sages' exposition, and questions how the small thing "mah" comes specifically through the large number "me'ah."
section.t: B)
And it is explained in many places regarding the study of "do not read,"
that the interpretation according to its simple meaning is through the content of the interpretation that the Sages expounded.
Based on this, the language "do not read" will be understood, which implies negating the simple interpretation,
for the intention in this is
that it is impossible for this interpretation to exist except through the expounded interpretation.
Based on this,
in our case – "Do not read 'mah' but rather 'me'ah',"
that through "me'ah" one comes to "mah."
And one must understand,
for the word "mah" indicates that the matter
(being discussed)
is a small thing,
and in the language of the Gemara
"a minor matter,"
whereas "me'ah" is
a large number, even the completeness of number,
so that in order to reach completeness, much work is needed
[and likewise it is also regarding the one hundred blessings in their simple sense,
that in order to recite one hundred blessings every day, even on Shabbos and Yom Tov
(and similarly on a fast day),
special effort is required],
and how can they say that in order to come to "mah"
(a minor matter)
it is specifically through "me'ah"
(the matter of completeness that comes through work).
